What We Do

Full-Service Vascular / Vein Care Revenue Cycle Management

Vein center billing requires precise distinction between medically necessary and cosmetic venous procedures, correct ablation CPT code selection by technique, imaging guidance documentation, and prior authorization compliance. PMEX manages every element from the procedure report to payment posted.

Endovenous Ablation Coding

EVLA (36478) and RFA (36473) codes coded by technique from the procedure report.

Sclerotherapy Billing

Chemical ablation (36465 to 36468) billed per the injected vein type and size.

Duplex Ultrasound Billing

Venous duplex (93970 to 93971) billed separately from the procedure on mapping visits.

Medical Necessity Documentation

Conservative treatment failure documentation compiled for prior authorization.

Phlebectomy Coding

Ambulatory phlebectomy (37765 to 37766) coded by number of incisions from the report.

Imaging Guidance Add-Ons

76937 (ultrasound guidance) billed when documented alongside vascular access procedures.

Common Vascular / Vein Care Billing Problems

Each problem below is one PMEX resolves before it costs you revenue.

EVLA and RFA coded interchangeably when the technique determines the correct CPT code.

PMEX reads the procedure report to confirm ablation technique (laser vs. radiofrequency) and applies the correct code.

Prior authorization denied because conservative treatment documentation is incomplete.

PMEX compiles compression stocking compliance and conservative treatment history before submitting every venous ablation authorization.

Sclerotherapy billed at the wrong code level based on vein diameter.

PMEX confirms vein type and size from the procedure note and applies the correct sclerotherapy code per the treated vein category.

Cosmetic spider vein sclerotherapy billed to medical insurance without a covered diagnosis.

PMEX routes cosmetic venous procedures to patient billing and medical necessity procedures to insurance based on diagnosis and documentation.

Duplex ultrasound not billed on mapping visits preceding venous ablation.

PMEX identifies duplex ultrasound mapping visits from the clinical schedule and submits 93970 or 93971 on qualifying diagnostic visits.

Ultrasound guidance add-on not billed when documentation confirms guidance was used.

PMEX bills 76937 (ultrasound guidance for vascular access) alongside access procedures when guidance is documented.

Denial Management

Top Denial Patterns in Vascular / Vein Care Billing

Vein centers lose 18 to 32 percent of revenue to medical necessity documentation gaps, ablation code errors, and cosmetic vs. medical misclassification.

PATTERN 01

Venous Ablation Denied, Conservative Treatment Not Documented

Endovenous laser ablation of great saphenous vein billed. Commercial payer denies: prior authorization was obtained but the auth documentation did not include evidence of 6 to 12 weeks of compression stocking use. Authorization voided retroactively.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX compiles conservative treatment documentation before submitting venous ablation prior authorization, including compression stocking prescription, duration of use, and physician documentation of symptom persistence despite conservative therapy.

PATTERN 02

EVLA Coded as RFA, Wrong Technique Billed

Radiofrequency ablation performed (36473). Billing team submits endovenous laser ablation code (36478). Payer adjudicates at the incorrect rate. On audit, the procedure report confirms RFA technique. Compliance exposure and rate adjustment required.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX reads the operative report to confirm ablation technique before selecting the CPT code. EVLA (36478 to 36479) and RFA (36473 to 36474) are distinct procedures with distinct codes. Technique is confirmed before every ablation claim.

PATTERN 03

Spider Vein Sclerotherapy Billed to Medical Insurance

Cosmetic spider vein injection (36468) submitted to commercial medical insurance. Denied as cosmetic exclusion. Spider veins do not meet medical necessity criteria on most commercial plans. No ABN was issued. No patient collection option created before the service.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX categorizes venous procedures by medical necessity before billing. Cosmetic spider vein sclerotherapy is routed to patient billing or self-pay. Medical insurance is billed only when the diagnosis and documentation support medically necessary treatment.

Questions

Vascular / Vein Care Billing Questions Answered

Most commercial payers require documentation of symptomatic varicose veins (aching, swelling, skin changes), duplex ultrasound confirming reflux, and 6 to 12 weeks of failed conservative treatment with compression stockings. We compile this documentation before submitting the authorization.

Endovenous laser ablation uses CPT 36478 (first vein) and 36479 (each additional vein). Radiofrequency ablation uses CPT 36473 (first vein) and 36474 (each additional vein). The technique is confirmed from the operative report before code selection.

Yes, on diagnostic mapping visits that occur on a different date of service than the procedure. Duplex ultrasound on the same day as an ablation may be bundled depending on the payer. We confirm billing eligibility per date of service.

Medical venous procedures treat symptomatic varicose veins with documented reflux and functional impairment. Cosmetic procedures address spider veins or telangiectasias without functional symptoms. Medical procedures are billed to insurance; cosmetic procedures are billed to the patient.

Ambulatory phlebectomy (37765) covers the first to five veins. Each additional vein uses 37766. We count the number of treated veins from the procedure report and bill the correct quantity.

Within 30 days, with venous procedure coding workflows and prior authorization tracking active from day one.
